lc-01-salvador-humilde.context: Mary and Joseph are in Bethlehem and find no room at the inn. In the fields nearby, ordinary shepherds spend the night watching their flocks when they receive the great news.
lc-01-salvador-humilde.focusQuestion: How do you receive the news that the Savior was born for you too?
lc-01-salvador-humilde.keywordGloss: Name given to the child born in Bethlehem, who brings God's salvation to the people.
facts: The child was laid in a manger because there was no room at the inn.
There were shepherds in the fields watching their flocks at night.
The glory of the Lord shone around the shepherds and they were filled with great fear.
The angel announces good news of great joy for all the people.
In the city of David the Savior was born, who is Christ the Lord.

lc-02-misericordia.context: Luke 15 brings together stories of searching: one sheep out of a hundred and one coin out of ten. The one who loses does not give up on what was lost and celebrates on finding it.
lc-02-misericordia.focusQuestion: How do you respond to a God who seeks those who are lost?
lc-02-misericordia.keywordGloss: God goes out to meet the lost and rejoices when there is repentance.
facts: The man with a hundred sheep loses one and searches until he finds it.
On finding the sheep, he puts it on his shoulders with joy.
He gathers friends and neighbors to rejoice with him.
There is more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents.
The woman lights the lamp, sweeps the house and searches carefully for the drachma.
There is joy before the angels of God over one sinner who repents.

lc-03-caminho-jerusalem.context: The disciples argue about greatness and exclusivity as Jesus nears the decisive time. He corrects both impulses and firmly resolves to go to Jerusalem.
lc-03-caminho-jerusalem.focusQuestion: What does greatness on the way with Jesus mean to you?
lc-03-caminho-jerusalem.keywordGloss: The destination Jesus walks toward with firm resolve, in obedience to the Father.
reflectionPrompts: No revenge on those who reject
facts: Whoever receives a child in Jesus' name receives Jesus himself.
The least among all is the one who is truly great.
John says they forbade a man because he did not go with the group.
Jesus says whoever is not against the disciples is for them.
Jesus firmly resolved to go to Jerusalem as his ascension drew near.
The Samaritans did not receive Jesus because he was going to Jerusalem.

lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao.context: After the resurrection, Jesus is with the disciples, eats in front of them and returns to the Scriptures. Before leaving, he announces the mission that will begin in Jerusalem.
lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao.focusQuestion: How do the Scriptures help you understand who Jesus is today?
lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao.keywordGloss: The Christ suffers, rises on the third day and sends witnesses to all nations.
facts: Jesus took the food and ate in the presence of the disciples.
Everything written about Jesus in the Law, the Prophets and the Psalms had to be fulfilled.
Jesus opened the disciples' understanding so they could grasp the Scriptures.
The Christ had to suffer and rise from the dead on the third day.
Repentance for the remission of sins would be proclaimed to all nations.
The disciples are witnesses of these things.

lc-boss-revisao.context: This challenge revisits Luke: the Savior announced to shepherds, the search for the lost, the decision to go to Jerusalem and the risen Christ who sends witnesses.
lc-boss-revisao.focusQuestion: Which part of Jesus' journey in Luke most calls you to follow him today?
lc-boss-revisao.keywordGloss: Jesus is born humbly, seeks the lost, goes to Jerusalem and wins by rising again.
facts: In the city of David the Savior was born, who is Christ the Lord.
There is more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents.
Jesus firmly resolved to go to Jerusalem.
The Christ had to suffer and rise on the third day.
Repentance would be proclaimed to all nations, beginning at Jerusalem.
The disciples are witnesses of these things.
